## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: the new `CRITERION_HINT` tells every user to leave out "shall", but when `require_shall=True` the validator rejects any criterion without " shall ". This review read the full diff, `app/criteria.py`, `tests/test_criteria.py` and `config.example.yml`. No project policy files are listed in the manifest. The new `BULLET_HINT` wording matches the `"- "` prefix check at `app/criteria.py:5`.

## Changes
The pull request rewords `CRITERION_HINT` to ask for direct action bullets without the word "shall", and rewords `BULLET_HINT` to show the exact `- ` prefix. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — Make CRITERION_HINT match the require_shall option — With `require_shall=True`, a user who follows the new hint and writes `- Save the result` gets the criterion rejected. The hint says "Write criteria as direct action bullets without the word shall.", but `accepts_criterion` returns `" shall " in text` when `require_shall` is set (`app/criteria.py:7-8`). The existing test `test_plain_bullet_under_shall_option` (`tests/test_criteria.py:20-21`) asserts exactly this rejection. `require_shall` is a documented setting in `config.example.yml:1`, and the PR body says the validator options are kept. — Deployments that enable `require_shall` now show a hint that leads users to write criteria the validator always rejects, with nothing telling them what to change. — Fix: Make the hint depend on the option, for example a separate hint or a function of `require_shall` that asks for "shall" when it is required. Another option is to drop the "without the word shall" clause so the hint holds for both settings.
